name: TWA 30 (Hubble)
blurb: TWA 30, a pair of young stars in the TW Hydrae Association, seen by Hubble.
label: twa30field-hubble
story: Two young stars of the TW Hydrae Association share this field: TWA 30A and its wide companion TWA 30B, which hides behind its own disk, seen edge-on. Both show signs of accretion disks and outflows, and Hubble looked here to resolve their disks and jets.

claims.text: TWA 30A and B are TW Hydrae Association members with evidence of accretion disks and outflows
The field was placed to put both stars near the center of the detector
The program aimed to resolve disks and jets in this low-mass binary
TWA 30B is a wide companion of TWA 30
TWA 30B is hidden by its disk, which is viewed edge-on
TWA 30 is a T Tauri star
